facts.text: Cluttered and reflective surroundings are environments full of metal, water, walls and piles that bounce sensor signals in confusing ways, producing apparent echoes from nowhere and hiding real objects.
facts.quote: Cluttered and reflective surroundings are environments full of metal, water, walls and piles that bounce sensor signals in confusing ways, producing echoes from nowhere and hiding real objects.

facts.text: Steel structures, other machines, the machine's own body, wet ground, rock faces and material piles reflect radar, lidar and ultrasonic sensor signals on job sites.
facts.quote: Steel structures, other machines, the machine's own body, wet ground, rock faces and material piles all reflect signals.

facts.text: Mirror-like surfaces such as wet ground can send a lidar beam away so that no return is received, or reflect the scene so that mirror points appear below the surface.
facts.quote: Mirror-like surfaces such as wet ground send a lidar beam away so nothing returns, or reflect the scene so that mirror points appear below the surface [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The booklet's strongest evidence for simulation of cluttered and reflective surroundings concerns a radar on a wheel loader in a hall, where thin metal pillars were highly reflective while walls behaved differently.
facts.quote: The booklet's strongest evidence is a radar on a wheel loader in a hall: thin metal pillars were highly reflective while walls behaved differently

facts.text: In the wheel-loader radar example in a hall, the synthetic image matched reality only after hand-built geometry and tuned materials.
facts.quote: the synthetic image matched reality only after hand-built geometry and tuned materials

facts.text: In the wheel-loader radar simulation in a hall, some real double reflections were still missing.
facts.quote: some real double reflections were still missing [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The booklet found no validated simulation of material piles, highwalls, large steel structures or the machine's own body for any sensor.
facts.quote: Material piles, highwalls, large steel structures and the machine's own body were not found validated in simulation for any sensor [Chapter 6].

facts.text: A simple "ray hits mesh equals detection" model will not reproduce sensor behavior around large metal bodies.
facts.quote: A simple "ray hits mesh equals detection" model will not reproduce behavior around large metal bodies [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Clutter caused real false alarms from a haul truck's own rear tires and protruding structures; field reports also identify rock piles, berms and vegetation as alarm sources.
facts.quote: a haul truck's own rear tires and protruding structures triggered false alarms, and field reports name rock piles, berms and vegetation

facts.text: A berm used by a driver as a bump stop is a real object with no collision risk, motivating the booklet's distinction between false alarms and nuisance alarms.
facts.quote: a berm the driver uses as a bump stop is a real object with no collision risk, which is why the booklet separates false from nuisance alarms [Chapters 4, 7].

facts.text: The booklet treats radar and ultrasonic simulation of off-road clutter as low credibility until validated against the company's own measurements.
facts.quote: The booklet treats radar and ultrasonic simulation of off-road clutter as low credibility until validated against the company's own measurements

facts.text: Bench stimulation equipment cannot reproduce multipath from metal structures.
facts.quote: multipath from metal structures is among the effects that bench stimulation equipment cannot reproduce either [Chapters 7, 9].
